itinerary: Day 1: Islamabad to Booni/Chitral, 12-hour AC transport, depart 12:30 AM
Day 2: Booni to Yarkhun (Broghil Valley) by 4x4 jeep, camp setup
Day 3: Yarkhun to Lashkargaz, trek begins
Day 4: Lashkargaz to Karambar Lake, explore and relax
Day 5: Reserve day for weather and small side treks
Day 6: Retrace from lake back to Yarkhun/Ishkarwaz after breakfast
Day 7: Drive to Chitral city, arrive ~5:00 PM
Day 8: Chitral to Islamabad, arrive 8-9 PM
pros: Satellite phone and tracking explicitly included for this remote route
Government NOC and permissions handled by operator
Built-in reserve day (Day 5) for weather and acclimatisation
Route genuinely reaches Karambar Lake (4272m) on Day 4
Transparent PKR pricing: PKR 110,000 per person from Islamabad
cons: Only one full day at the lake before retracing; short for such a long approach
Personal-luggage porter charged separately, not in base price
Emergency evacuation and personal insurance excluded
verdict: A focused, well-supported 8-day Broghil approach to Karambar Lake with rare safety extras (sat phone, permits) and honest PKR pricing. Best for those wanting a shorter, logistics-handled trip to the lake.
excludes: Personal-luggage porter, emergency evacuation, personal insurance, and miscellaneous expenses.

itinerary: Day 1: Arrive Islamabad, hotel transfer, evening briefing and gear check
Day 2: Islamabad to Gilgit, then Karimabad (Hunza), Baltit Fort
Day 3: Karimabad to Sost to Chipursan Valley (Zood Khun), camp near Wakhi village
Day 4: Trek to Yarzerech, meadows and streams, camp at base of cliffs
Day 5: Trek to Chillinji Base Camp (~4,400m), camp near glacier
Day 6: Acclimatization day, short hikes, pass preparation
Day 7: Cross Chillinji Pass (5,335m), descend to Ishkoman side
Day 8: Trek to Werthum Meadows, high pastures with wildlife
Day 9: Trek to Imit Village (Ishkoman), cultural experience and homestay
Day 10: Drive to Gilgit, free evening at bazaar, overnight hotel
Day 11: Gilgit to Islamabad, free time for shopping/sightseeing
Day 12: Departure, airport transfer
pros: Strong acclimatisation profile with a dedicated Day 6 before a 5,335m pass
Crosses high Chillinji Pass linking Chipursan to remote Ishkoman side
Cultural depth: Wakhi village camp and Imit Village homestay
Honest about being a seldom-visited, remote route
cons: Does NOT reach Karambar Lake; this is a Chillinji Pass trek, not a Karambar trek
No detailed inclusions list published on the page
Pricing in USD ($1400), no PKR or permit/sat-phone detail
verdict: A genuine high-pass crossing (Chillinji, 5,335m) into Ishkoman, but it is mismatched to a Karambar Lake search since the route never reaches the lake. Suitable only for buyers specifically wanting the Chillinji crossing.
excludes: Not specified on the page (no exclusions list published).

itinerary: Day 1: Islamabad, airport greeting, city tour, overnight
Day 2: Islamabad to Gilgit by early flight
Day 3: Gilgit to Darkot village, early-morning drive
Day 4: Darkot to Darkot base camp, distribute luggage among porters
Day 5: Base camp to Chikar via Darkot Pass, depart 8 AM
Day 6: Chikar to Lashkargaz, trekking into Broghil valley
Day 7: Lashkargaz to Laly Rabat across flat terrain
Day 8: Laly Rabat to Karamber Lake, reach the lake
Day 9: Free day at Karamber Lake, photography, horse and yak riding
Day 10: Karamber Lake back to Lashkargaz
Day 11: Lashkargaz to Ishkarwaz to Mastuj
Day 12: Mastuj to Chitral by road
Day 13: Chitral to Swat Valley by road
Day 14: Swat Valley to Islamabad via motorway
pros: Reaches Karamber Lake (4,300m) plus a full free day there on Day 9
Crosses Darkot Pass, a more adventurous route than a simple Broghil out-and-back
Porters and expert cook during the trek included
Domestic flights, transport and airport pick/drop all included
Acknowledges remoteness: 'one of the most isolated remote areas of Pakistan'
cons: No price published on the page
No satellite phone or emergency comms mentioned for this isolated route
Permits not specifically listed in inclusions
Tips for guide, drivers and porters are extra
verdict: The most adventurous itinerary here, combining the Darkot Pass with two days at Karamber Lake and good ground support. Weakened by no published price and no stated sat-phone or permit handling.
excludes: International flights, airport/departure taxes and visa fee, tips for guide/drivers/porters, and personal items.

itinerary: Day 1: Islamabad arrival, hotel transfer
Day 2: Drive to Chilas, 10-12 hrs
Day 3: Drive to Gilgit, 4-5 hrs
Day 4: Drive to Bort, 5-6 hrs
Day 5: Trek to Maturamdan, 5-6 hrs
Day 6: Trek to Waraghut, 5-6 hrs
Day 7: Trek to Sokhter Rabot, 5-6 hrs
Day 8: Trek to Shuyinj, 5-6 hrs
Day 9: Trek to Karambar Lake, 5-6 hrs
Day 10: Free day
Day 11: Trek to Ishkarwaz, 3-6 hrs
Day 12: Trek to Darkot An base camp, 3-5 hrs
Day 13: Trek to Rawat, 5-6 hrs
Day 14: Trek to Darkot, 3-5 hrs
Day 15: Drive to Gilgit and continue to Chilas, 6-7 hrs
Day 16: Drive to Islamabad, 8-10 hrs
Day 17: Transfer to airport
pros: Most complete full traverse: reaches Karambar Lake (Day 9) then crosses Darkot An
Cook, support staff, porters and gear (excluding personal) all included
Free day (Day 10) at the lake plus daily trek hours stated for pacing
cons: No altitudes given for Karambar Lake or the passes on the page
No satellite phone or emergency-comms reference for this remote traverse
Long 17-day commitment with multiple very long drive days
verdict: The fullest expedition-grade Karambar-to-Darkot traverse with strong licensed ground support and permits included. Held back by missing altitudes, no price, and no stated satellite/emergency comms.
excludes: Travel insurance, visa, international flights, tips, and miscellaneous personal items.
